name: DINER (Disorder-Invariant Implicit Neural Representation)
definition: A method that uses a learnable full-resolution hash-table to map input coordinates to a new space with more low-frequency components, allowing a small MLP to achieve high accuracy regardless of the input signal's arrangement order.
summary: DINER is a disorder-invariant implicit neural representation that uses a learnable hash-table to map coordinates, allowing the network to ignore input order and focus on fitting attribute manifolds.
